question: What is the main difference between rest and sleep?

options.A: Rest requires medication while sleep happens naturally without help
options.B: Rest is a calm, relaxed state while sleep is an altered state with reduced sensory activity
options.C: Rest only occurs at night while sleep can happen at any time of day
options.D: Rest involves reduced consciousness while sleep maintains full alertness

explanation: Think of rest as simply chilling out while you're still awake and aware. Sleep, on the other hand, is a deeper state where your brain tunes out the world around you so it can recharge. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h1)

question: Why is getting enough sleep so important for our patients in the hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will be discharged within forty-eight hours
options.B: It eliminates the need for expensive pain relief medications
options.C: It prevents patients from talking too much to the nursing staff
options.D: It speeds up physical healing and strengthens the body's immune defenses

explanation: When patients sleep well, their bodies can focus on repairing tissues and fighting off infections. Good rest is a powerful form of medicine! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which sleep stage is best known for helping the body physically recover and deeply relax its muscles?
explanation: Stage 3 is our deep sleep stage! This is when the body goes to work repairing tissues, building muscle, and healing. Essential for recovery. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h2)

question: What major activity happens inside the brain during Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep?

options.A: The body completely shuts down all metabolic processes
options.B: Heart rate and breathing drop to their lowest daily levels
options.C: Intense brain activity and vivid dreaming occur
options.D: Muscles become completely rigid and unable to move

explanation: Even though your body is resting, your brain is super active during REM sleep! This is when we dream and process our emotions and memories. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason why patients struggle to sleep in a hospital?

options.A: Comfortable room temperatures and soft lighting
options.C: Frequent nighttime vital sign checks by staff
options.D: Constant noise from equipment and hallway chatter

explanation: Hospitals are usually noisy, bright, and busy with checks—not exactly a peaceful spa! Comfortable conditions actually help patients sleep. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h3)

question: A patient on a water pill (diuretic) keeps waking up all through the night. Why is this happening?

options.A: The drug stimulates brain activity like caffeine
options.B: The medicine makes the patient urinate frequently
options.C: The medication causes severe joint pain
options.D: The pill induces sudden anxiety attacks

explanation: Diuretics make the kidneys produce more urine. Naturally, this means the patient has to make frequent trips to the restroom at night! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h3)

question: What is a common sign you might spot in a patient who hasn't been sleeping well over a few days?
explanation: When we lack sleep, our brains get sluggish and moody. Patients can easily become easily annoyed, forgetful, or mildly confused. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h4)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out about a newly admitted patient's usual sleeping habits?

options.A: Wait until the patient complains of exhaustion before asking questions
options.B: Ask the patient about their usual bedtime and morning wake time
options.C: Review the patient's chart for historical vital sign trends
options.D: Observe the patient sleeping for two hours during the afternoon shift

explanation: Just ask them! Talking directly to your patient about their normal routine helps you create a care plan that fits their natural body clock. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h4)

question: In nursing, what does 'bundling care' mean when it comes to helping patients sleep?

options.A: Administering all daily medications at the exact same morning hour
options.B: Wrapping the patient tightly in heavy wool blankets
options.C: Grouping multiple care tasks together to reduce the number of times a patient is woken up
options.D: Sharing night shift duties evenly between nurses and assistants

explanation: Instead of waking your patient up every hour for a different task, you combine vital signs, meds, and dressings into one visit. That way, they get longer stretches of uninterrupted sleep! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h5)

question: A patient complains that the hallway is too bright and noisy to sleep at midnight. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Explain that hospital noise is normal and the patient will get used to it
options.B: Move the patient to a bed located directly at the nurse's station
options.C: Close the patient room door and dim the overhead lights
options.D: Call the doctor immediately to request a strong sleeping pill

explanation: Simple environmental tweaks like pulling the curtains, dimming lights, and shutting the door work wonders before reaching for medications. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a great example of a non-drug (non-pharmacological) way to help a patient relax?

options.B: Ordering a stronger dose of painkiller
options.C: Administering a standard dose of zolpidem
options.D: Increasing the intravenous fluid infusion rate

explanation: A gentle back rub helps relieve tension and promotes relaxation naturally, without any medication side effects. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h6)

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful when giving sleeping pills to older adult patients?

options.A: Older adults process drugs faster, rendering the pills useless
options.B: Sleeping pills increase the risk of daytime drowsiness and accidental falls
options.C: Older adults are legally barred from taking sleeping medications
options.D: Sedatives always cause severe allergic reactions in senior patients

explanation: Sedatives can linger in an older adult's system, causing grogginess and unsteady legs during the day. This puts them at high risk for falls! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is a key sleep tip you can teach a patient who is getting ready for discharge?

options.A: Drinking two cups of strong coffee right before bedtime
options.B: Maintaining a consistent sleep and wake schedule every day
options.C: Watching television in bed until falling fast asleep
options.D: Eating a large, heavy meal immediately before resting

explanation: Going to bed and waking up at the same time trains the body's internal clock, making it much easier to fall and stay asleep. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h7)

question: Why should nurses advise patients to stay off their phones or TVs right before trying to sleep?

options.A: Watching shows late at night leads to weight gain
options.B: Screen use causes severe dehydration in the eyes
options.C: Electronic devices consume too much electricity in the bedroom
options.D: The bright light from screens tricks the brain into staying awake

explanation: The blue light from phone and TV screens blocks melatonin, the natural hormone that tells our brain it's time to sleep. Put the phone away for a better night's rest! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h7)
